summary: Open-RAG-Eval is an open-source project addressing a major RAG evaluation bottleneck: the nonscalable requirement for golden answers or golden chunks. Developed in collaboration with the University of Waterloo's Jimmy Lin lab, the framework uses LLM-based judges to provide automated, reference-free evaluation. The architecture begins with a set of queries (10 to 1000), which are processed through RAG connectors that collect chunks and answers from a RAG pipeline. Connectors currently exist for Vectara, LangChain, and LlamaIndex, with community contributions encouraged for others. The collected outputs are run through evaluators containing grouped metrics, producing evaluation files. Four primary metrics are featured. UMBRELA is a retrieval metric scoring chunks 0-3 (0=irrelevant, 3=dedicated to query with exact answer); University of Waterloo research shows it correlates well with human judgment. AutoNuggetizer is a generation metric operating in three steps: creating atomic units called nuggets, assigning vital/okay ratings and selecting top 20, then using an LLM judge to determine if each nugget is fully or partially supported by the RAG response. Citation faithfulness measures whether citations are fully supported, partially supported, or unsupported. Hallucination detection uses Vectara's model to check alignment between the response and retrieved content. A web-based UI at open-evaluation.ai allows users to drag and drop evaluation files for visual comparison of retrieval and generation scores across queries. The framework is fully open-source, with transparent metric methodologies.

sections.title: Introduction and Project Overview
sections.summary: Ofer Mendelevitch from Vectara introduces Open-RAG-Eval, an open-source project for quick and scalable RAG evaluation, with a QR code linking to the repository.

sections.title: Architecture and Connectors
sections.summary: Explains the framework's research backing (University of Waterloo, Jimmy Lin lab) and architecture: queries flow through RAG connectors (Vectara, LangChain, LlamaIndex) that collect chunks and answers, then evaluators run grouped metrics to produce evaluation files.

sections.title: Metrics Overview
sections.summary: Introduces four key metrics: UMBRELA for retrieval without golden chunks, AutoNuggetizer for generation, citation faithfulness, and hallucination detection using Vectara's model.

sections.title: UMBRELA Retrieval Metric
sections.summary: UMBRELA scores chunks 0-3 (0=irrelevant, 3=dedicated to query with exact answer). University of Waterloo research shows it correlates well with human judgment, enabling effective retrieval evaluation without golden chunks.

sections.title: AutoNuggetizer Generation Metric
sections.summary: AutoNuggetizer works in three steps: creating atomic nuggets, assigning vital/okay ratings and selecting top 20, then using an LLM judge to determine if each nugget is fully or partially supported by the RAG response.

sections.title: Citation Faithfulness and Hallucination Detection
sections.summary: Citation faithfulness measures if citations are fully, partially, or not supported. Hallucination detection uses Vectara's model to check if the entire response aligns with retrieved content.

sections.title: UI, Open Source, and Call to Action
sections.summary: Describes the UI at open-evaluation.ai for visualizing evaluation results by drag-and-dropping files. Emphasizes open-source transparency, available connectors, and invites community contributions for new connectors via issues or PRs.

demonstrations: Architecture diagram showing flow from queries through connectors, evaluators, to evaluation files

limitations: Raw evaluation files tend to be complex to read directly, necessitating the UI for interpretation
